answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before it can transact: every agent locks collateral at a shared registry vertex, and that stake is slashed if one operator spins up duplicate identities. Like a quill signing each attestation with a unique key, the stake ties reputation to one costly identity, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes. In a sparse tundra of trust, where strangers rarely meet twice, this makes fakery expensive while honest agents keep earning from a single verified identity.
